propositions: File-level caused_by auto-derivation via git blame agrees with recorded edges 43% of the time, disagrees 7%, and abstains 50% across 88 closed bugs with caused_by edges, with no provenance field distinguishing blamed from explicitly supplied edges.

On 8 bugs with independently proven root-cause origins, the deriver reproduced zero correct attributions and named an innocent party confidently once (1 wrong-target, 7 abstained), dominated by unmet obligation and carrier-commit defect shapes.

The deriver's abstentions (50% population, 7/8 subsample) concentrate in hard defect shapes (unmet obligations, carrier commits, omissions) where file-majority blame fails closed rather than guesses, but provenance ambiguity makes confidence uncomputable for consumers.

No distinguishing marker exists on caused_by edges to identify whether an attribution came from git blame or explicit supply, preventing metrics from weighting them differently despite different reliability profiles.
History drift confounds accuracy measurement: 3 fixing commits no longer resolve, 8 tickets lack file_impact paths, reformat/move carriers can dissolve majorities that existed at close time.

A single-target batch (ed5c target with five different derived targets across five tickets) demonstrates that file-blame scatters family-level attributions when all five edges were supplied and point to one origin.
